title: Relative power-series evaluation and its closed-fibre diagram
statement:
Let $f:(A,\mathfrak m,K)\to(B,\mathfrak n,L)$ be a local homomorphism of nonzero commutative Noetherian local rings [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring], with residue fields $K=A/\mathfrak m$, $L=B/\mathfrak n$ and induced inclusion $\iota:K\hookrightarrow L$. Suppose $A,B$ are complete for their maximal ideals [def-weil-pbc-adically-complete-ring]. Fix residue sections $a:K\to A$, $b:L\to B$ with $b\iota=fa$, an integer $e\geq0$, generators $x_1,\ldots,x_e$ of $\mathfrak m$, and a continuous surjective local map $q:R=K[[X_1,\ldots,X_e]]\to A$ with $q|_K=a$ and $q(X_i)=x_i$ [def-weil-pbc-multivariate-power-series]. Assume $C=B/\mathfrak mB$ is complete regular local [def-weil-regular-scheme] of finite Krull dimension $s\geq0$ [def-weil-pbc-krull-dimension-ring]. Let $\pi:B\to C$ be the quotient map. There are $t_1,\ldots,t_s\in\mathfrak n$ such that $\bar t_i=\pi(t_i)$ generate the maximal ideal of $C$, and a continuous isomorphism of local $L$-algebras $\rho:L[[T_1,\ldots,T_s]]\xrightarrow{\sim}C$ with $\rho|_L=\pi b$ and $\rho(T_i)=\bar t_i$. Put $S=L[[X_1,\ldots,X_e,T_1,\ldots,T_s]]$, let $j:R\to S$ extend coefficients by $\iota$ and retain the $X$ variables, and let $p:S\to L[[T_1,\ldots,T_s]]$ set all $X$ variables to zero. Then $S$ is Noetherian complete local with maximal ideal $(X,T)S$, $j$ is local, $p$ is surjective with $\ker p=(X)S$, and there is a continuous surjective local map $v:S\to B$ satisfying
$$v|_L=b,\quad v(X_i)=f(x_i),\quad v(T_i)=t_i,\quad vj=fq,\quad \pi v=\rho p.$$
In particular $\ker v\subseteq(X)S$. No flatness of $f$, characteristic restriction, or finite type hypothesis is imposed.

source.place: Agent-formulated coefficient-preserving presentation diagram: Tag 07NQ (proposition-fs-flat-fibre-fs), proof of (2) implies (3), special-fibre diagram before the kernel identity; algebra.tex Tag 0C0S (lemma-regular-complete-containing-coefficient-field), clause (2) and proof. Extracted from original steps 5--7 of lem-trf-relative-cohen-flat-presentation; explicit evaluation and setting-X-to-zero identities are the refinement.

proof.text: Write $\mathfrak p=\mathfrak n/\mathfrak mB$ for the maximal ideal of $C$. Indeed $\mathfrak mB\subseteq\mathfrak n$ because $f$ is local, and $C/\mathfrak p=B/\mathfrak n=L$. By the definition of regular local ring, choose $s$ generators $\bar t_i$ of $\mathfrak p$; choose lifts $t_i\in\mathfrak n$. The map $c=\pi b:L\to C$ induces the identity on this residue field. Apply [lem-trf-regular-complete-coefficient-coordinates] with $k=L$, $d=s$, and this generating list. Its hypotheses are exactly the assumed Noetherian regularity, finite dimension and completeness of $C$, and it gives the required continuous local $L$-algebra isomorphism $\rho$, preserving both coefficients and the selected parameters.

Apply the field case of [lem-weil-pbc-power-series-field-cohen-regular-complete] to $K$ with $e$ variables and to $L$ with $e+s$ variables. Thus the maximal ideals of $R,S$ are $\mathfrak r=(X)R$ and $\mathfrak h=(X,T)S$, and both rings are complete Noetherian local rings. The coefficientwise map $j$ is a ring map by the finite convolution formula for multiplication; it sends $X_i$ to $X_i$, hence $j(\mathfrak r)\subseteq\mathfrak h$ and $j(\mathfrak r^N)\subseteq\mathfrak h^N$, so it is local and continuous. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-power-series-quotient-variables] over $L$ with $d=e+s$ and $i=e$: it gives precisely $p$, its surjectivity and $\ker p=(X)S$. On monomials $p(\mathfrak h^N)\subseteq(T)^N$, so $p$ is continuous.

source.place: Tag 032C (remark-Noetherian-complete-local-ring-universally-catenary), power series over a field; coefficient and variable-quotient refinements stated in the cited nodes.

proof.text: All $f(x_i)$ and $t_i$ lie in $\mathfrak n$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-power-series-adic-evaluation] to $\alpha=b:L\to B$, $I=\mathfrak n$, and this $e+s$ element list. Completeness of $B$ gives a continuous ring map $v:S\to B$ with $v|_L=b$, $v(X_i)=f(x_i)$ and $v(T_i)=t_i$. As $\mathfrak h$ is generated by these variables, $v(\mathfrak h)\subseteq\mathfrak n$; hence $v$ is local.

source.place: Tag 07NL (lemma-power-series-ring-over-Cohen-fs), power-series universal property in the proof, as made explicit by the cited evaluation node.

proof.text: Let $J=v(\mathfrak h)B=(f(x_1),\ldots,f(x_e),t_1,\ldots,t_s)B$. For $z\in\mathfrak n$, express $\pi(z)=\sum_i\bar u_i\bar t_i$ in $C$, and lift the finitely many $\bar u_i$ to $u_i\in B$. Then $z-\sum_i u_it_i\in\ker\pi=\mathfrak mB=(f(x_1),\ldots,f(x_e))B$, proving $\mathfrak n\subseteq J$; the reverse inclusion holds because all generators lie in $\mathfrak n$. Thus $J=\mathfrak n$. The composite $S\xrightarrow v B\to B/J=L$ is surjective since on constant series $b$ is a residue section. Now apply [lem-weil-pbc-complete-source-surjective-mod-ideal] with source ideal $\mathfrak h$: $S$ is precomplete by step 2, and $B$ is $J$-adically Hausdorff because $J=\mathfrak n$ and its assumed completeness includes separatedness. This proves that $v$ is surjective.

source.place: Tag 0315 (lemma-completion-generalities), complete-source surjectivity method; precise ring-map form in the cited node and Mathlib/RingTheory/AdicCompletion/Functoriality.lean, lines 447-459.

proof.text: The maps $vj,fq:R\to B$ are continuous: $j,v,q$ are continuous and $f(\mathfrak m^N)\subseteq\mathfrak n^N$. They agree on $K$, since $b\iota=fa$, and on every $X_i$, where both take the value $f(x_i)$. Uniqueness in [lem-weil-pbc-power-series-adic-evaluation], with target ideal $\mathfrak n$, gives $vj=fq$. Likewise $\pi v,\rho p:S\to C$ are continuous for the variables-adic and $\mathfrak p$-adic topologies: $\pi(\mathfrak n^N)\subseteq\mathfrak p^N$ and $p$ is continuous by step 2. They agree on $L$ by $\rho|_L=\pi b$, on $X_i$ by $\pi f(x_i)=0$, and on $T_i$ by $\rho(T_i)=\bar t_i$. Apply the same uniqueness assertion with target ideal $\mathfrak p$ (for which $C$ is assumed complete) to obtain $\pi v=\rho p$.

source.place: Tag 07NN (lemma-embed-map-Noetherian-complete-local-rings), power-series maps in its proof; coefficient-preserving diagram identities verified here by the cited evaluation uniqueness.

proof.text: For $F\in\ker v$, the second identity gives $\rho(p(F))=\pi(v(F))=0$. Since $\rho$ is injective, $p(F)=0$; step 2 then gives $F\in\ker p=(X)S$. This proves the kernel inclusion. All arguments allow empty variable lists: if $s=0$, $\rho:L\to C$ is the coefficient isomorphism of step 1; if $e=0$, $p$ is the identity and the inclusion says $v$ is injective. If both vanish, it is the coefficient isomorphism $L\to B$.

This is the first split of a statement node: 0 new nodes, the statement is identical to live and stmt_deps are unchanged. proof_deps equals the union of the step uses. The item is still unsplit in live and side-live, so no parallel group has superseded it, and there is no re-split note. I read all 8 cited statements and every step checks out. Step 1: C is a nonzero Noetherian quotient with maximal ideal p=n/mB; lifts of generators of p lie in n; πb induces id_L on C/p, so lem-trf-regular-complete-coefficient-coordinates gives ρ with k=L, d=s. Step 2: R and S come from the field branch of the power-series structure node; j is local and continuous; p and ker p=(X)S come from quotient-variables with i=e. Step 3: adic-evaluation into the n-complete B with α=b gives v; v is local because v^{-1}(n)=h. Step 4: J=v(h)B=n by lifting coefficients of π(z), since ker π=mB=(f(x))B; the complete-source criterion then applies with the correct image ideal, and n-Hausdorffness follows from completeness. Step 5: both squares follow from evaluation uniqueness (α=bι with I=n, and α=πb with I=p); the values on K/L, X_i and T_i were checked. Step 6: the kernel chase through injective ρ. Edge cases e=0, s=0 and inseparable L/K pass; I also tested A=K[[x]], B=L[[x,t]]. Sources read: Stacks 0C0S (algebra.tex 45036ff) and the 07NQ (2)⇒(3) diagram, where flatness is used only at the end and is not needed here; no SGA is cited. Duplicate search over dag/nodes found nothing that states this diagram. The four pbc tool_uses are generic power-series and completion foundations, and I accept them.
